title: SSP-1 — Document Subject And Association Delivery
summary: project optional folder, Work and Series authoring subjects into focused associations, Manage cues and reporting inputs
content_html:
SSP-1 — Document Subject And Association Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as SSP-1, the first complete subject implementation in Sub-Scope Publishing. SSP-0 — Projects Subject Assignment Foundation Delivery supplies the accepted read-only subject Info projection and capability-selected assignment modal on SSC-1's shipped sub_scope_customisation contract. Sub-Scope Publishing Concept And Architecture owns the typed-subject, cardinality, projection, access, refresh, and failure contracts implemented by this delivery.

SSP-1 establishes source-to-manifest identity before Project State, Resolver Tokens, collection-aware transfer, catalogue-document reporting, or public Work/Series metadata consume it.

The feature-level sense check is settled by the architecture. SSP-1.0 confirms implementation fit and current owners only; it does not reopen the one-working-collection, optional-metadata, or non-gating publication decisions.

Complete Outcome

All working documents may remain in dotlineform/projects. Its documents follow the authoring convention of zero or one of folder_path, work_id, and series_id. folder_path remains Projects-specific; work_id and series_id become optional document-level catalogue association fields understood in any managed or published collection.

The source reader projects normalized subject state and deterministic folder-, Work-, or Series-to-document associations without inferring identity. Several documents may declare one subject. Missing metadata is ordinary. Malformed or conflicting catalogue declarations are excluded from associations and exposed as non-blocking authoring evidence; they never prevent saving, Copy, viewability changes, or publication.

Manage indexes show a compact subject cue derived from the normalized manifest row: folder icon for folder_path, catalogue icon for work_id or series_id with an exact accessible label, and no icon when no subject is declared. The cue is not lifecycle status, eligibility, or target-existence proof. The same exact Work/Series association output becomes the input to curator-facing catalogue document coverage; Studio Works reporting retains presentation and scheduling ownership. SSP-1 adds no Resolver rendering, Project State scan, copy workflow, public reverse lookup, or catalogue-page presentation.

Subject assignment is a dotlineform/projects authoring convenience because that configured sub-scope's registered customisation advertises the assignable subject group; SSP-1 adds no literal Projects name check. It extends the SSP-0 modal to None, Folder, Work, and Series, reusing Catalogue target search for the last two choices while Info remains read-only. SSP-1 establishes the collection-independent read projection that SSP-4 later applies when it explicitly creates analysis/works; SSP-4 owns acceptance of the copied read-only subject and capability boundary.

Accepted SSP-0 Input

SSP-1 extends the shipped authoring_subject group, exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} Info projection, POST /docs/assign-field-group revision receipt, focused Projects modal, async status containment, exact-detail refresh, and generic Edit metadata separation. The current group owns folder_path; SSP-1 adds work_id and series_id to that server declaration and extends the existing modal response validation rather than creating another assignment route or Info editor.

Folder keeps the current DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR-relative normalization. Work and Series reuse the Catalogue target picker and submit canonical scalar IDs through the same exact confirmed mutation. The Projects browser contribution continues to derive availability from the resolved group ID. Collection-independent Work/Series read projection remains separate from this Projects-only authoring capability so SSP-4 can later configure analysis/works as read-only subject metadata.

Delivery Discipline

SSP-1 extends the Projects registration on SSC-1's shared customisation contract, adds one bounded document-level Work/Series metadata reader, and composes the current manifest and Manage-index owners. It must not introduce a second metadata framework, graph database, relationship query language, new working sub-scope, nested sub-scopes, or cross-system lifecycle synchronization.

SSP-1.0 is a short scope-and-spec sanity gate. It confirms the current broad owners, likely blast radius, deliverables, risks, and stop condition without freezing an exact implementation. Each implementation step ends with focused evidence and an independent code/diff review before the next step begins. If the shared subject representation requires widespread generic builder changes rather than bounded source-reader and manifest composition, stop for review.

Delivery Steps

SSP-1.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [ ] Sanity-check optional Projects/Work/Series authoring subjects, focused associations, and Manage index cues against SSC-1's accepted registered aspects, source readers, manifest builders, Index presentation, document-location projection, and targeted collection rebuild model; resolve only contradictions that would change the result.
  • [ ] Confirm the broad blast radius across shared and Projects-specific front matter, customisation validation/import, Manage manifests, focused association products, Index cues, locations, and downstream SSP transfer dependencies.
  • [ ] Confirm the deliverables: optional scalar subjects, deterministic exact-target associations, non-blocking invalid/conflict evidence, Manage-only folder/catalogue cues, public isolation, focused evidence, and concise durable owner updates.
  • [ ] Stop for review if the result requires a second metadata framework, widespread generic builder changes, live relationship scans during manifest projection, or another boundary excluded above. Do not produce an exact file inventory, line estimate, frozen implementation, fixture implementation, or complete test architecture at this gate.

Checkpoint: a concise sanity note confirms the spec, scheduling dependency, broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, public/Manage boundary, and stop condition. Stop before implementation approval.

SSP-1.1 — Implement Authoring Subjects And Manage Cues

  • [ ] Extend the accepted SSP-0 authoring_subject declaration and existing Projects modal from None/Folder to one optional None, Folder, Work, or Series group; add work_id and series_id to the server-owned field set, reuse Catalogue target search and picker components, and retain the exact assignment route, passive Info view, and capability-derived availability.
  • [ ] Retain scalar-string folder_path metadata read/write, import handling, and exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} targeting in dotlineform/projects; add shared scalar-string work_id and series_id reads without tying them to a collection.
  • [ ] Project normalized none, valid folder, valid Work, valid Series, malformed, and conflicting authoring states while preserving raw canonical source and keeping every state saveable, copyable, and publishable.
  • [ ] Produce deterministic folder-, Work-, and Series-to-documents associations for valid declarations, with exact document-location descriptors usable by later Studio Works coverage reporting, without reading live folder or catalogue relationships during manifest projection or broadening Work/Series identity through membership.
  • [ ] Add Manage-index folder and catalogue subject cues from normalized manifest metadata, with exact accessible labels and no icon for a no-subject document; use a bounded authoring warning for malformed/conflicting declarations.
  • [ ] Keep local paths, private association products, invalid-source detail, and Manage cue data out of public products.

Checkpoint: focused source metadata, Projects customisation, import, manifest, association, Index presentation, location, targeted-build, lifecycle-non-gating, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms folder meaning remains Project-specific, Work/Series metadata remains collection-independent, no-subject publication survives, cues remain observational, and Project State/public reverse lookup retain downstream ownership. Stop before SSP-1.2.

SSP-1.2 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused customisation, source metadata, import, manifest, location, public-isolation, targeted-build, lint, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Prove several documents may declare one subject while ordinary creation, Copy, viewability, and publication remain valid with no declaration.
  • [ ] Prove no subject is inferred from title, filename, body, route, selected row, report host, or UI state.
  • [ ] Perform the independent final code/delivery review, reconcile the completion claims with exact evidence and omissions, and record any bounded follow-up trigger.
  • [ ] Update SSP-2, SSP-3, SSP-4, and SSP-5 with the accepted subject, association, Manage-cue, and transfer schemas before any of those deliveries begins.

Completion Evidence

  • dotlineform/projects remains the one normal working collection and accepts zero or one folder/Work/Series declaration by authoring convention.
  • work_id and series_id are optional document metadata in any collection; neither absence, malformed input, nor a conflict prevents ordinary lifecycle or publication.
  • Manifests project normalized authoring state and preserve zero-to-many association cardinality for valid declarations.
  • The Work/Series association product supplies exact document targets and current location descriptors for the curator catalogue-document coverage requirement; the eventual Studio Works route remains presentation-owned.
  • Manage indexes show observational folder/catalogue cues without creating another report, subject picker, or eligibility control.
  • Manage products retain exact working document targets; public products contain only allowed public-safe locations and no local folder paths.
  • Association and cue generation performs no Project State scan, Resolver expansion, copy, Registry mutation, or public Work/Series payload mutation.
  • The accepted transfer contract makes generic work_id/series_id retention and Projects-specific folder_path omission explicit.
  • Subject quick assignment is available only through the assignable field group registered by the exact dotlineform/projects customisation; SSP-4 later proves the configured analysis/works copy uses this delivery's read projection without gaining that group.

The Sub-Scope Publishing feature owns sequencing. SSP-1 stops after source, manifest, and focused association foundations; each downstream consumer retains its own delivery gate.
